strategyPosture: Hold core exposure; do not chase the crypto-leverage rip into a 14.8 VIX. The actionable watchlist is the nuclear/power dislocation, where accelerating SMR permitting collides with double-digit selloffs — wait for price stabilization before probing.

themes.counterRead: Policy and contracting momentum is accelerating while prices fall — the exact setup where the story is underpriced, not overpriced. But sentiment-driven selloffs can overshoot: BWXT RSI 38.1 and NXT RSI 39.8 are weak, not washed out. Probe only on stabilization, not on the narrative alone.
themes.dataAnchor: SMR permitting is an active HIGH-signal event (4 news hits: GE Vernova/Hitachi/Samsung SMRs for Europe; Centrus/Antares multi-year HALEU deal). Yet nuclear names lead the 1-month laggards: OKLO -11.2%, SMR -10.4%. Deeper dislocations flagged FULL_SIGNAL and sentiment-driven: NXT -50.7% from 52w high, BWXT -39%, VST -36%. Beneficiaries per signal detection: LEU, BWXT, CCJ, VST, CEG.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power: permitting accelerates, stocks sell off
themes.narrative: AI data-center power demand is a crisis and SMR permitting is being fast-tracked — the market story says nuclear-adjacent names should be ripping.
themes.watchFor: OKLO or SMR closes above its 10-day high on volume above 1.5x the 20-day average.

themes.counterRead: This is the crowded long: vertical moves in decay-prone leverage products while the VIX sits at 14.81 (-7.5% over the month). The debasement bid may be real, but the vehicle is lottery-like here. Let it wash out before expressing any crypto view — IBIT, not 2x single-stock leverage.
themes.dataAnchor: 1-month leaders are all crypto/leverage: CONL +34.6% (+23% today alone), BMNR +27.7% (+8.2% today), COIN +21.5% (+11.9% today), IBIT +18.2%. Over the same month the VIX fell 7.5% to 14.81 — no fear premium is being paid for these moves.
themes.label: Crypto-leverage rip into a complacent VIX
themes.narrative: The debasement trade is back — Bitcoin proxies and leveraged single-stock ETFs are vertical, implying the market expects the liquidity bid to continue.
themes.watchFor: A single-day drop greater than 15% in CONL or BMNR — a leverage washout, not a buy signal until volume capitulates.

themes.counterRead: Nobody is fooled by the index level: the 8.66-point gap between SPY (-1.6% from high) and the average Mag7 name (-10.26%) is the market's real breadth read. With lending standards UNKNOWN, this cannot be classified as rotation vs. rollover — so size as if either is possible: no new mega-cap concentration until the gap resolves.
themes.dataAnchor: Market concentration readState is DIVERGENCE_UNCONFIRMED: Mag7 average 10.26% below 52-week highs vs SPY only 1.6% below — an 8.66-point divergence gap. META is the strongest Mag7 name (-0.3% from high); TSLA the weakest (-24.2%). Credit context is missing (lending standards zone UNKNOWN), so rotation cannot be confirmed.
themes.label: Index calm masks Mag7 divergence
themes.narrative: SPY at 762.94, just 1.6% off its high, suggests an orderly market — but the average mega-cap growth name is 10% off its high.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap narrowing below 5 points (breadth healing) or widening past 12 points (rollover risk).

themes.counterRead: Credit is the adult in the room: HY OAS at 2.70% says there is no funding stress behind the small-cap drawdown. If credit stays this calm, the IWM -5.9% month is a sentiment discount on rate-sensitive equities, not a solvency warning — a probe candidate, not a short.
themes.dataAnchor: IWM is -5.86% over one month (-0.48% today) while HY option-adjusted spread sits at 2.70% — extremely tight, signaling zero credit stress. 10Y at 4.94% with a +27bp 2s10s curve and 2.61% real 10Y: restrictive but stable, not spiking.
themes.label: Small caps sag while credit shrugs
themes.narrative: Higher-for-longer is crushing small caps — IWM's 6% monthly slide says rate-sensitive equities are pricing real pain.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS widening past 3.5% — credit confirming the small-cap stress would flip this from opportunity to warning.

themes.counterRead: Sentiment-driven, not fundamental-driven — but RSI readings in the high 30s/low 40s mean no capitulation yet. These are watchlist names (APP at -58.7% and HUBS at -58.9% are deep value territory on sentiment alone), not entries: wait for the RSI to wash out or the trend to turn.
themes.dataAnchor: SaaS/software dislocations flagged FULL_SIGNAL and sentiment-driven: HUBS -58.9% from 52w high (RSI 42.1), APP -58.7% (RSI 39.8), NOW -30.4% (RSI 52.9, trend actually +6.5% 1m), DDOG -21.5% (RSI 48.9). RDDT -42.8% (RSI 45.1). NFLX, a holding, is -10.3% on the month.
themes.label: Software derating without a fundamental verdict
themes.narrative: Software is being derated across the board — the narrative says AI is eating SaaS margins and multiples simultaneously.
themes.watchFor: Any of HUBS/APP printing RSI below 30 (capitulation) or reclaiming the 50-day average (trend repair).

watchFor: OKLO or SMR closes above its 10-day high on >1.5x average volume (nuclear stabilization).
VIX closes above 20 (complacency break — cut levered exposure).
HY OAS widens past 3.5% (credit confirming equity stress).
Mag7/SPY divergence gap below 5pts (healing) or above 12pts (rollover).
CONL or BMNR single-day drop >15% (leverage washout).
whereWaveBuilds: The highest-convexity move is a snapback in the nuclear/power complex: SMR permitting plus HALEU contracting is accelerating into -10% monthly selloffs and -36% to -51% dislocations — the first green volume day there is the probe trigger; the risk is the crypto-leverage rip reversing into a low VIX and dragging sentiment with it.
